_doc: Reviewed registry of every params.fields key a COMPOSER consumes.
tools/composer_param_lint.py errors on any composer-consumed key not
registered here — so adding one forces the question this registry
encodes: is the key MUSIC or MECHANISM, and which ledger entry / canon
musical-content    — the value IS music (a contour, a fade formula);
the model can learn it; preferred (C1/C10/C14).
mechanism-knob     — reproduces a per-member player mechanism the
write stream demands (C19 wedges etc.). Each is
a standing DECONSTRUCTION candidate; note it.
temporal-dispatch  — WHEN play runs, not what it plays (C18/C24/C31).
A key a musician could not read that is NOT a mechanism demanded by
the write stream is the principle-section-8 leak in param clothing.

digi_player.licensed_by: NONE — meets principle section-8's test exactly (the composer's choice of which 6502 to emit depends on USF content -> _digi_player_registry). The old C7-category-C citation was WRONG: C7-C covers the PCM sample data (FLAC sidecars, fine), not the player choice. Re-assessed 2026-08-16, note corrected 2026-08-20 (backlog item 5).
digi_player.note: LATENT, not active: a library of one (1 corpus carrier, 4k-era Chimera; 1 registry entry). Owner-reviewed TRIPWIRE: the SECOND digi engine migrated (e.g. Galway $D418 4-bit) must PARAMETRIZE (a real technique enum like digi { technique: wavetoggle_1bit | volume_4bit, rate: N }; the composer synthesizes the player) — NEVER add registry row two. DigiCode's addresses are composer layout and must not be reachable from USF even by name.

vib_ramp.note: CONVERSION TRIGGER (principle section-4 parameter-vs-kind, review 2026-08-13): 'step' vs 'step_full' differ by an ORDERED shift amount (freq_hi>>1 vs freq_hi), not a category. At two values the enum is readable; if a THIRD swell rate ever appears, convert to a numeric field (e.g. swell_shift) instead of minting a fourth enum value.
